sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: 'It's a bit scary' - Jewish students explain classroom security measures Schools and colleges in England will be required to recognise antisemitism as a distinct category of harm and take explicit action against it following a major review, the BBC understands.
sentences.article_title: Schools should recognise antisemitism as distinct form of harm, review says

sentences.text: It means anti-Jewish hatred would be treated as a specific safeguarding risk rather than being dealt with through existing measures to stop racism and bullying.
sentences.article_title: Schools should recognise antisemitism as distinct form of harm, review says

sentences.text: The government-commissioned review into antisemitism in education is also expected to recommend dedicated training for teachers, more consistent recording and reporting of incidents, and better education about antisemitism and modern-day Jewish life.
sentences.article_title: Schools should recognise antisemitism as distinct form of harm, review says

sentences.text: The BBC understands it will also call for stronger guidance on political impartiality for teachers.
sentences.article_title: Schools should recognise antisemitism as distinct form of harm, review says

sentences.text: The review, led by former Ofsted chief inspector Sir David Bell, is due to be presented to Parliament on Wednesday.
sentences.article_title: Schools should recognise antisemitism as distinct form of harm, review says

sentences.text: The government is expected to accept all 27 recommendations.
sentences.article_title: Schools should recognise antisemitism as distinct form of harm, review says

sentences.text: It was launched amid growing concern about antisemitism in the UK, following a series of high-profile incidents including the attack at Heaton Park synagogue in Manchester in October 2025 , in which two men were killed.
sentences.article_title: Schools should recognise antisemitism as distinct form of harm, review says

sentences.text: The BBC revealed in August that the Bell review had found Jewish schoolchildren were experiencing regular harassment and abuse.
sentences.article_title: Schools should recognise antisemitism as distinct form of harm, review says

sentences.text: It also found that headteachers of some Jewish schools were spending more of their time dealing with security arrangements than educational matters.
sentences.article_title: Schools should recognise antisemitism as distinct form of harm, review says

sentences.text: Recent figures from the Community Security Trust, an organisation which provides security advice and support to the Jewish community, showed a spike in antisemitic incidents at schools.
sentences.article_title: Schools should recognise antisemitism as distinct form of harm, review says

sentences.text: It found in the first half of 2026 that antisemitism in schools had reached the highest level ever recorded for the first six months of any year.
sentences.article_title: Schools should recognise antisemitism as distinct form of harm, review says

sentences.text: It jumped by 59%, from 112 reported incidents in the first half of 2025 to 178 recorded over the same period in 2026.
sentences.article_title: Schools should recognise antisemitism as distinct form of harm, review says

sentences.text: The review is also expected to recommend that the government sets up a type of hotline where school leaders can access immediate advice on tackling antisemitism.
sentences.article_title: Schools should recognise antisemitism as distinct form of harm, review says

sentences.text: Bell told the BBC: "This is not just a report for Jewish children in Jewish schools.
sentences.article_title: Schools should recognise antisemitism as distinct form of harm, review says

sentences.text: This is for all children and young people in all schools and colleges.
sentences.article_title: Schools should recognise antisemitism as distinct form of harm, review says

sentences.text: Spencer Lewis, the executive headteacher of Yavneh College, said that security was an "innate part" of his role.
sentences.article_title: Schools should recognise antisemitism as distinct form of harm, review says

sentences.text: "When you come in in the morning, there are high gates, high fences, lots of security cameras.
sentences.article_title: Schools should recognise antisemitism as distinct form of harm, review says

sentences.text: We have four full-time security staff.
sentences.article_title: Schools should recognise antisemitism as distinct form of harm, review says

sentences.text: And it sort of just becomes part of what you do," he said.
sentences.article_title: Schools should recognise antisemitism as distinct form of harm, review says

sentences.text: "We think about it a lot." Staff and pupils told the BBC they have become so used to these measures that they barely notice them anymore.
sentences.article_title: Schools should recognise antisemitism as distinct form of harm, review says

sentences.text: Lock-in - or "in-vacuation" - drills for dealing with intruders have become second nature, even to the youngest pupils.
sentences.article_title: Schools should recognise antisemitism as distinct form of harm, review says

sentences.text: "It's a bit scary sometimes, but you know you're safe," said Livi, a Year 6 pupil.
sentences.article_title: Schools should recognise antisemitism as distinct form of harm, review says

sentences.text: "It's sad that we can't be equal to everyone else, but people don't like us just because of the way we are," added her classmate, Sadie.
sentences.article_title: Schools should recognise antisemitism as distinct form of harm, review says

sentences.text: A group of a dozen older pupils who spoke to the BBC said that while they feel safe inside school, hearing about antisemitic attacks in the UK, including reports of pupils at other Jewish schools being harassed on their commute and at sports fixtures, has left them feeling targeted.
sentences.article_title: Schools should recognise antisemitism as distinct form of harm, review says

sentences.text: Some said that they were reluctant to wear skullcaps or necklaces featuring the Star of David – a Jewish symbol – outside school.
sentences.article_title: Schools should recognise antisemitism as distinct form of harm, review says

sentences.text: "Other religions get to be out and wear their necklaces and be proud - I don't get why Jewish people can't do it as much," said Year 9 pupil Ilan.
sentences.article_title: Schools should recognise antisemitism as distinct form of harm, review says

sentences.text: In response to the recommendations, the government is also expected to encourage schools to adopt the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance (IHRA)'s working definition of antisemitism, although it cannot make it compulsory.
sentences.article_title: Schools should recognise antisemitism as distinct form of harm, review says

sentences.text: The definition is supported by mainstream Jewish organisations and has been adopted by 47 countries, including the UK, as well as most British universities.
sentences.article_title: Schools should recognise antisemitism as distinct form of harm, review says

sentences.text: However, some of the IHRA definition's examples of antisemitic behaviour have proven controversial.
sentences.article_title: Schools should recognise antisemitism as distinct form of harm, review says

sentences.text: The Board of Deputies of British Jews said that adopting the IHRA definition would provide schools with a tool "to deepen understanding of contemporary antisemitism".
sentences.article_title: Schools should recognise antisemitism as distinct form of harm, review says

sentences.text: The Department for Education has declined to comment before the review is published.
sentences.article_title: Schools should recognise antisemitism as distinct form of harm, review says

sentences.article_title: King praises Strait of Hormuz peace efforts at glittering banquet

sentences.text: Oman is a key Middle Eastern partner of the UK, and one of the countries along the Strait of Hormuz, with the red carpet rolled out for Sultan Haitham bin Tarik Al Said.

sentences.text: The King's banquet speech praised the country's "noble efforts in trying to keep open one of the world's most important shipping routes".
sentences.article_title: King praises Strait of Hormuz peace efforts at glittering banquet

sentences.text: And over a dinner of pheasant and quince, he praised Oman's diplomatic mediation in the conflict with Iran to establish "where common ground might be found".

sentences.text: The Strait of Hormuz, one of the world's most vital shipping lanes, has been effectively closed since then.

sentences.text: King Charles, Queen Camilla, Prince William and Catherine and Princess Anne were among the royals on duty at Windsor for the state visit.

sentences.text: It was the first state banquet for Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who was seated next to the Omani academic and novelist, Jokha Alharthi.

sentences.text: It was a table laden with elaborate candelabra and polished decorations, with five glasses per setting, and even the surface of the salt had an imprint of the cypher of King Charles.

sentences.text: The hot summer meant a bumper crop of pomegranates in the Windsor Castle gardens, and the fruits were placed on the table alongside the floral decorations.
sentences.article_title: King praises Strait of Hormuz peace efforts at glittering banquet

sentences.text: The King's speech, delivered to 160 guests in English with some quotes in Arabic, expressed his approval that his son Prince William had worked on an expedition project alongside the Sultan's son.

sentences.text: "There can be few happier symbols of success than a living relationship being passed from one generation to the next," said the King.

sentences.text: But he had stolen some of the attention from the state visit, with the publication of an interview in which he said he wanted to reconcile with his family .
sentences.article_title: King praises Strait of Hormuz peace efforts at glittering banquet

sentences.text: "Some people don't want it to work out.
sentences.article_title: King praises Strait of Hormuz peace efforts at glittering banquet

sentences.text: With everything else that's going on in the world, the most important thing is to reconcile - that's the key point," Prince Harry told GQ in New York.

sentences.text: There was wine available at the banquet, but with Muslim guests of honour, the traditional banquet cocktail was replaced by a non-alcoholic spiced coffee drink.

sentences.text: During his visit to the UK, the Sultan's delegation will be meeting UK business representatives.

sentences.article_title: 60 years on: The Aberfan disaster through the eyes of those who survived

sentences.text: Sixty years on, the tragedy remains woven into the nation's collective memory, a day of unimaginable loss that reshaped a community and changed attitudes to industrial safety across Britain.

sentences.text: At 09:15 on 21 October 1966, an ordinary school morning was shattered when a coal tip above Aberfan collapsed. 144 people died following the Aberfan landslide in October 1966 Black slurry thundered down the mountainside, engulfing Pantglas Junior School and nearby homes.

sentences.text: Within moments, 144 people were dead, including 116 children, on what was the last day of school before the half-term holiday.

sentences.text: Moon, the MP for Camborne and Redruth, is listed on Companies House as the co-director of a training company called Autoswot , external , which last filed accounts in June 2021.
sentences.article_title: Second Labour MP suspended over Covid loan repayments

sentences.text: Government Bounce Back Loans of up to £50,000 were made available to support small businesses during the pandemic, but a government report found the scheme was vulnerable to fraud and error.
sentences.article_title: Second Labour MP suspended over Covid loan repayments

sentences.text: In August, Labour MP Bayo Alaba was suspended after queries about a Covid-era loan, and a third MP, James McMurdock, quit Reform in 2025 after questions about eligibility for loans he received.
sentences.article_title: Second Labour MP suspended over Covid loan repayments

sentences.text: Bounce back loans worth a total of £46bn were issued when the scheme was launched in May 2020, making it the biggest of the government's pandemic-era loan schemes.
sentences.article_title: Second Labour MP suspended over Covid loan repayments

sentences.text: Each one had a 100% government guarantee, meaning taxpayers' cash was used to pay back banks if the companies failed, but the Covid counter-fraud commissioner later found total fraud and error estimated at up to £2.8bn to the public purse.
sentences.article_title: Second Labour MP suspended over Covid loan repayments

sentences.text: Autoswot had been set up in June 2019, a year before the loans became available, and at that time had forecast revenues of more than £200,000.
sentences.article_title: Second Labour MP suspended over Covid loan repayments

sentences.text: Moon stressed he had applied for the maximum loan of £50,000 within the rules, regularly seeking professional advice about its obligations, and would provide documents to the Labour Party investigation into the matter.
sentences.article_title: Second Labour MP suspended over Covid loan repayments

sentences.text: He said the loan was used to pay for "staffing and other essential business costs" during the pandemic and partial repayments were made until the company ceased trading in late 2022.
sentences.article_title: Second Labour MP suspended over Covid loan repayments

sentences.text: The BBC understands that Moon was repeatedly assured in writing by Companies House that no accounts needed to be filed after the company applied to be struck off, but that guidance was incorrect.
sentences.article_title: Second Labour MP suspended over Covid loan repayments

sentences.text: Moon, who was first elected in the 2024 Labour landslide following a career in communications and marketing, said the business folded due to unforeseen external market pressures and "despite the best efforts of staff".
sentences.article_title: Second Labour MP suspended over Covid loan repayments

sentences.text: He said: "In order for these matters to be looked into, I have voluntarily referred myself to the Labour Party's investigations process and will cooperate fully with this process.
sentences.article_title: Second Labour MP suspended over Covid loan repayments

sentences.text: "The loan application was made in good faith, and the information provided, including the company's turnover forecast, was accurate and properly based.
sentences.article_title: Second Labour MP suspended over Covid loan repayments

sentences.text: "I will continue to work hard every day representing my constituents while this party process is ongoing." A Labour Party spokesperson confirmed Moon had referred himself for investigation.
sentences.article_title: Second Labour MP suspended over Covid loan repayments

sentences.text: "The Labour Party expects the highest standards from our elected representatives and we have robust processes in place to ensure those high standards are upheld," they said.
sentences.article_title: Second Labour MP suspended over Covid loan repayments

sentences.text: "We cannot comment further while the investigation is ongoing." This is the second investigation the Labour Party has launched into the loans, with Alaba, the MP for Southend East and Rochford , also referring himself for investigation over loans made to a real estate company, Alaba Properties.
sentences.article_title: Second Labour MP suspended over Covid loan repayments

sentences.text: At the time, Alaba said: "There has been no attempt to avoid my financial obligations, and I am wholeheartedly committed to ensuring that the liability is met in full." McMurdock, who now sits as an independent, was the first MP to be questioned over bounce back loans given to two fitness companies worth £70,000.
sentences.article_title: Second Labour MP suspended over Covid loan repayments

sentences.text: In 2025 McMurdock said all his business dealings had been compliant with the rules, adding that after taking "specialist legal advice" he had decided "to continue my parliamentary career as an independent MP".
sentences.article_title: Second Labour MP suspended over Covid loan repayments

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: UK has 'responsibility to back allies and protect civilians', says defence secretary The UK will deploy RAF Typhoon jets to defend Saudi Arabia in response to escalating Houthi missile and drone attacks, the government has said.
sentences.article_title: UK to deploy jets to defend Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks

sentences.text: The defensive mission will help defend Saudi cities and infrastructure -  a move authorised by Prime Minister Andy Burnham - against aerial attacks by the Iran-backed group.
sentences.article_title: UK to deploy jets to defend Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks

sentences.text: It follows Houthi attacks on the Saudi capital Riyadh, as well as on energy sites on the country's coast.
sentences.article_title: UK to deploy jets to defend Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks

sentences.text: "These aircraft will operate in a defensive role and will not conduct offensive strikes against the Houthis," Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said in a written statement on Tuesday.
sentences.article_title: UK to deploy jets to defend Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks

sentences.text: An RAF Typhoon in flight (file image) The Houthis are locked in a civil war with Yemen's internationally recognised government, which is backed by Saudi Arabia and were ousted by the group from capital, Sanaa, in 2014.
sentences.article_title: UK to deploy jets to defend Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks

sentences.text: Since September, Saudi Arabia has been struggling to defend its skies from Houthi attacks after a ceasefire of sorts in Yemen broke down.
sentences.article_title: UK to deploy jets to defend Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks

sentences.text: The Houthis launched a fresh offensive against Yemen's officially recognised government and seized effective control of the crucial Bab al Mandab strait.
sentences.article_title: UK to deploy jets to defend Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks

sentences.text: Government forces - backed by Saudi aircover - mounted a counter offensive and the Houthis in turn struck targets deep in Saudi territory.
sentences.article_title: UK to deploy jets to defend Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks

sentences.text: The Houthis successfully hit Saudi infrastructure including the King Khalid airport, energy facilities and key ports.
sentences.article_title: UK to deploy jets to defend Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks

sentences.text: Saudi authorities said last week that 19 people had been killed in Houthi attacks on the kingdom's airports.
sentences.article_title: UK to deploy jets to defend Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks

sentences.text: One missile strike on Riyadh's international airport on 10 October killed 13 people and injured 308 others – the deadliest attack in Saudi Arabia in more than a decade.
sentences.article_title: UK to deploy jets to defend Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks

sentences.text: This video can not be played Footage from inside Riyadh airport on 10 October shows the moment the strike hit Houthis have been retaliating for strikes on territory that they control in western Yemen, including the capital Sanaa.
sentences.article_title: UK to deploy jets to defend Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks

sentences.text: More than 70 security personnel were killed earlier this week in a Houthi missile strike on a camp in Yemen's central province of Shabwa.
sentences.article_title: UK to deploy jets to defend Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks

sentences.text: A spokesman for the Saudi-backed Yemeni armed forces said the Iran-backed group launched three ballistic missiles at al-Alam camp near Ataq city.
sentences.article_title: UK to deploy jets to defend Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks

sentences.text: The Houthis' military spokesman said they had targeted "Saudi enemy concentrations".
sentences.article_title: UK to deploy jets to defend Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks

sentences.text: According to the Houthi-run health ministry in north-western Yemen, Saudi air and artillery strikes have killed at least 141 people and injured 395 since 3 September.
sentences.article_title: UK to deploy jets to defend Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks

sentences.text: The government's health ministry, meanwhile, said last week that at least 1,282 people had been killed in the conflict across Yemen since 6 August.
sentences.article_title: UK to deploy jets to defend Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks

sentences.text: Saudi Arabia has struggled to bring down incoming missiles and drones because so much of its air defence capability was used up against Iranian attacks earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: UK to deploy jets to defend Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks

sentences.text: The sheer size of the country also makes it hard to provide comprehensive air defence.
sentences.article_title: UK to deploy jets to defend Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks

sentences.text: The UK warplanes will not only help Saudi Arabia defend its skies, but they will also free up the country's own aircraft to carry out offensives strikes against the Houthis.
sentences.article_title: UK to deploy jets to defend Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks

sentences.text: The UK will also deploy military advisers and an RAF A400M transport aircraft to support the movement of defence equipment within Saudi Arabia.
sentences.article_title: UK to deploy jets to defend Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks

sentences.text: It is already providing Saudi Arabia with defence support equipment to protect against aerial attacks and air-to-air refuelling for defensive Saudi operations.
sentences.article_title: UK to deploy jets to defend Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks

sentences.text: The refuelling has now been extended by 90 days.
sentences.article_title: UK to deploy jets to defend Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks

sentences.text: In a separate statement, Streeting said the targeting of Riyadh airport "shows the lengths the Houthis are going to escalate the situation in the region".
sentences.article_title: UK to deploy jets to defend Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks

sentences.text: "That's why today I have approved further UK military support," the defence secretary added.
sentences.article_title: UK to deploy jets to defend Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks

sentences.text: Streeting also pointed to violence in the Gulf disrupting energy supplies and increasing costs for families and businesses.
sentences.article_title: UK to deploy jets to defend Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks

sentences.text: Earlier this month, Houthi military spokesman Brig Gen Yahya Saree vowed to continue the "escalating operations deep inside Saudi Arabia".
sentences.article_title: UK to deploy jets to defend Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks

sentences.text: Who are the Houthis and what do they want?

sentences.text: The UK audit regulator has confirmed it is leading inquiries into accounting irregularities at Manchester City.
sentences.article_title: Audit regulator looking into Manchester City accounting

sentences.text: The Financial Reporting Council confirmed in a letter to the House of Commons business select committee it had taken over "regulatory consideration" of the case from the Institute of Chartered Accountants in England and Wales on 30 September.
sentences.article_title: Audit regulator looking into Manchester City accounting

sentences.text: No formal investigation has started, but the FRC is making inquiries into the case.
sentences.article_title: Audit regulator looking into Manchester City accounting

sentences.text: It comes after Manchester City were found guilty by an independent commission of all charges relating to breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons, including by artificially inflating the club's financial position by more than £900m.
sentences.article_title: Audit regulator looking into Manchester City accounting

sentences.text: City are appealing the verdict.
sentences.article_title: Audit regulator looking into Manchester City accounting

sentences.text: The FRC has greater resources, and greater powers, to apply sanctions if it does find evidence of violations.
sentences.article_title: Audit regulator looking into Manchester City accounting

sentences.text: It routinely oversees accounting standards at bigger institutions such as listed public companies, but not football clubs.
sentences.article_title: Audit regulator looking into Manchester City accounting

sentences.text: The FRC can look into the conduct of BDO, Manchester City's auditors, to ask whether the audit was in line with the rules.
sentences.article_title: Audit regulator looking into Manchester City accounting

sentences.text: It can also apply sanctions to individuals such as directors or employees of the Etihad club, if they are members of professional accountancy bodies.
sentences.article_title: Audit regulator looking into Manchester City accounting

sentences.text: BDO is the UK's fifth-biggest accounting firm, but claims to be a market leader in football, advising more Premier League and Championship clubs than any other firm.
sentences.article_title: Audit regulator looking into Manchester City accounting

sentences.text: The independent commission which looked into Manchester City found that the club gave a "misleading impression" of the scheme used to disguise the origin of shareholder funds injected into the club to its auditors, who were "unaware" of the scheme.
sentences.article_title: Audit regulator looking into Manchester City accounting

sentences.text: Manchester City have said they will appeal against the commission's decision, arguing that it contains "material errors, of law, principle and fact and is unsafe".
sentences.article_title: Audit regulator looking into Manchester City accounting

sentences.text: Liam Byrne, chair of the business select committee, called for greater powers for the FRC to look into similar cases.
sentences.article_title: Audit regulator looking into Manchester City accounting

sentences.text: He wrote on X: "The regulator's letter exposes gaps in its ability to compel evidence from the club and pursue directors who fall outside its disciplinary rules.
sentences.article_title: Audit regulator looking into Manchester City accounting

sentences.text: "This raises serious questions about the powers available to hold companies and directors to account.
sentences.article_title: Audit regulator looking into Manchester City accounting

sentences.text: "The government has a responsibility to explain why reforms to close these gaps were abandoned - and what will now be done to strengthen accountability." Man City confirm appeal against guilty verdict
sentences.article_title: Audit regulator looking into Manchester City accounting

sentences.text: Jamie Collins (pictured) was ambushed and killed after returning home from university A student who stabbed his housemate more than 30 times in a masked ambush has changed his murder plea to guilty.
sentences.article_title: Student who stabbed housemate 30 times admits murder

sentences.text: Zack Coughlan, 23, attacked Jamie Collins, 21, in an alleyway near the garden of their home on 8 April and then left his body outside for eight hours before calling police.
sentences.article_title: Student who stabbed housemate 30 times admits murder

sentences.text: A murder trial had been under way at Bristol Crown Court because Coughlan initially denied the charge, although he did admit killing Collins.
sentences.article_title: Student who stabbed housemate 30 times admits murder

sentences.text: He told jurors he stabbed Collins because he feared his housemate would kill him .
sentences.article_title: Student who stabbed housemate 30 times admits murder

sentences.text: However, Coughlan, of Cleve Road, Filton, has now changed his plea to guilty and will be sentenced for murder on Wednesday.
sentences.article_title: Student who stabbed housemate 30 times admits murder

sentences.text: Describing him as "a sensitive and caring young man", Collins' family said he had been "looking forward to finishing his journey" at the University of the West of England (UWE) and returning home to Swansea "in a matter of weeks".
sentences.article_title: Student who stabbed housemate 30 times admits murder

sentences.text: "His passion for equality stood out to everyone who knew him.
sentences.article_title: Student who stabbed housemate 30 times admits murder

sentences.text: His unapologetic inclusivity will be his legacy for all of us.
sentences.article_title: Student who stabbed housemate 30 times admits murder

sentences.text: We know he was heading for a hugely successful future following his engineering and robotics degree," they added.
sentences.article_title: Student who stabbed housemate 30 times admits murder

sentences.text: Coughlan initially tried to blame masked attackers for his housemate's murder The men were both final-year robotics students at the UWE and lived together in a house in Filton, owned by Coughlan.
sentences.article_title: Student who stabbed housemate 30 times admits murder

sentences.text: During the trial, Coughlan claimed he was fearful of Collins , telling jurors he was "barely able to think" when he lay in wait for his housemate to return from university before stabbing him repeatedly.
sentences.article_title: Student who stabbed housemate 30 times admits murder

sentences.text: Coughlan then left his housemate to die in the alleyway behind their home before cycling away on the victim's bike to dispose of bloodstained evidence.
sentences.article_title: Student who stabbed housemate 30 times admits murder

sentences.text: He dumped the bike at a nearby retail park, bought a change of clothes and threw his bloodstained clothing in a pond, in carrier bags weighed down with bricks.
sentences.article_title: Student who stabbed housemate 30 times admits murder

sentences.text: Coughlan's DNA was found on bloodstained clothing recovered from a nearby pond On returning home he ate pizza and played video games, claiming he "had to disconnect" from what happened.
sentences.article_title: Student who stabbed housemate 30 times admits murder

sentences.text: He did not call 999 for another five hours.
sentences.article_title: Student who stabbed housemate 30 times admits murder

sentences.text: The entire attack was caught on CCTV Coughlan had installed himself, which also captures the moment he staged the discovery of Collins' body.
sentences.article_title: Student who stabbed housemate 30 times admits murder

sentences.text: Jurors were told he later rewatched this footage five times.
sentences.article_title: Student who stabbed housemate 30 times admits murder

sentences.text: Det Ch Insp Lucy Edgeworth, of the major crime investigation team, said "all the evidence suggests" the killing was a "pre-planned, cold-blooded execution".
sentences.article_title: Student who stabbed housemate 30 times admits murder

sentences.text: She said despite Coughlan claiming his housemate's political views had become more extreme and that he had talked about killing Coughlan, the motive for the murder was "not clear".
sentences.article_title: Student who stabbed housemate 30 times admits murder

sentences.text: "We know there was a dispute about rent.
sentences.article_title: Student who stabbed housemate 30 times admits murder

sentences.text: We know that they held different political views.
sentences.article_title: Student who stabbed housemate 30 times admits murder

sentences.text: But none of those things make any sense to why somebody would carry out such a horrific crime," she said.
sentences.article_title: Student who stabbed housemate 30 times admits murder

sentences.text: This video can not be played Killer's 999 call claiming housemate's body found cold Edgeworth pointed out inconsistencies in Coughlan's story, including claims he had injured his hands climbing a tree after the incident, which she called "slightly odd".
sentences.article_title: Student who stabbed housemate 30 times admits murder

sentences.text: She added the defendant's blood had been found on Collins' recovered bike because he had likely injured himself in the "ferocious and horrendous" attack.
sentences.article_title: Student who stabbed housemate 30 times admits murder

sentences.text: "The retrieval of the clothing from the pond, again, all forensically linked Zach to that crime.
sentences.article_title: Student who stabbed housemate 30 times admits murder

sentences.text: So it was a really interesting and complex forensic picture," she said.
sentences.article_title: Student who stabbed housemate 30 times admits murder

sentences.text: In a statement issued outside court, surrounded by Collins' family, Edgeworth described the murder as "meticulously planned".
sentences.article_title: Student who stabbed housemate 30 times admits murder

sentences.text: "The brutal nature of what he did cannot be underestimated," she said.
sentences.article_title: Student who stabbed housemate 30 times admits murder

sentences.text: "Rather than calling for medical help he did everything to protect himself.
sentences.article_title: Student who stabbed housemate 30 times admits murder

sentences.text: Judge Justice Linden said Coughlan's partial defence of manslaughter by reason of loss of control could not be left to the jury to consider as part of their deliberations on the murder charge.
sentences.article_title: Student who stabbed housemate 30 times admits murder

sentences.text: He told the jury: "You will have just heard that the defendant has changed his plea to the indictment to guilty.
sentences.article_title: Student who stabbed housemate 30 times admits murder

sentences.text: "That means that he now admits the charge of murder.
sentences.article_title: Student who stabbed housemate 30 times admits murder

sentences.text: "I would like, on behalf of us all, to thank you for the service that you have given in this case." This video can not be played CCTV footage shows how the attack unfolded In a statement issued following the verdict, Collins' family said his death had affected them in a "deep, profound and lasting way".
sentences.article_title: Student who stabbed housemate 30 times admits murder

sentences.text: They said: "As a family we have had to explain repeatedly to people what has happened.
sentences.article_title: Student who stabbed housemate 30 times admits murder

sentences.text: "Every time we do so it reinforces the pain of him having been killed so suddenly, and in such a senseless and brutal way.
sentences.article_title: Student who stabbed housemate 30 times admits murder

sentences.text: The university described him as a "valued member" of the robotics community and an active member of student societies.
sentences.article_title: Student who stabbed housemate 30 times admits murder

sentences.text: "He was a natural engineer, keen in robotics, a hard worker and only weeks away from completing his degree," said UWE Bristol vice-chancellor Steve West.
sentences.article_title: Student who stabbed housemate 30 times admits murder

sentences.text: "The details which have emerged during the trial are shocking, and particularly difficult for several of his university friends who were called as witnesses.
sentences.article_title: Student who stabbed housemate 30 times admits murder

sentences.text: "The number of friends and university staff who attended both Jamie's memorial and the court trial is testament to how much he was cared for." Follow BBC Bristol on Facebook , external , X , external and Instagram , external .
sentences.article_title: Student who stabbed housemate 30 times admits murder

sentences.text: Rio Ngumoha, aged 18 years and 52 days, became the youngest Liverpool player to either score or assist for the club in the Champions League In a game of seven goals, none were scored by Rio Ngumoha - but this was his night.
sentences.article_title: The night 'ruthless' Ngumoha came of age for Liverpool

sentences.text: The 18-year-old was simply a class apart from the rest in Liverpool's 4-3 win over Villarreal.
sentences.article_title: The night 'ruthless' Ngumoha came of age for Liverpool

sentences.text: It is over a year since Ngumoha burst on to the scene for Liverpool with a memorable stoppage-time winner at Newcastle.
sentences.article_title: The night 'ruthless' Ngumoha came of age for Liverpool

sentences.text: He has been in and out since then, impressing in flashes and even going on to make his England debut earlier this season.
sentences.article_title: The night 'ruthless' Ngumoha came of age for Liverpool

sentences.text: But this performance was different, inspiring his team to a memorable comeback win in the Champions League.
sentences.article_title: The night 'ruthless' Ngumoha came of age for Liverpool

sentences.text: By the time the teenager was replaced in the 74th minute, with Bradley Barcola taking over, the chants of "Rio, Rio, Rio" had repeatedly rung around Anfield.
sentences.article_title: The night 'ruthless' Ngumoha came of age for Liverpool

sentences.text: It was quite the sight to see Alisson embrace Ngumoha shortly after the young man was given Uefa's player of the match award.
sentences.article_title: The night 'ruthless' Ngumoha came of age for Liverpool

sentences.text: "It's up there with one of the best [games] I've played.
sentences.article_title: The night 'ruthless' Ngumoha came of age for Liverpool

sentences.text: I enjoyed myself out there and the team helped me a lot," Ngumoha told Amazon Prime.
sentences.article_title: The night 'ruthless' Ngumoha came of age for Liverpool

sentences.text: "Whenever I get the ball and there's an opportunity to go one versus one, or two versus one, I believe in myself to do it.
sentences.article_title: The night 'ruthless' Ngumoha came of age for Liverpool

sentences.text: I'll just keep going and be ruthless." Liverpool were woeful for much of the first half as they trailed Villarreal by two goals, but Ngumoha took responsibility and began to turn the tide.
sentences.article_title: The night 'ruthless' Ngumoha came of age for Liverpool

sentences.text: After Alexis Mac Allister pulled one back, Ngumoha found space to dink in a delightful ball that was met by Ronald Araujo for an equaliser.
sentences.article_title: The night 'ruthless' Ngumoha came of age for Liverpool

sentences.text: Ater the break, Ngumoha - as he had done all evening - waltzed past Sergi Cardona to set up Mac Allister to give Liverpool the lead.
sentences.article_title: The night 'ruthless' Ngumoha came of age for Liverpool

sentences.text: Florian Wirtz added what proved to be a vital fourth.
sentences.article_title: The night 'ruthless' Ngumoha came of age for Liverpool

sentences.text: Ngumoha inspires Liverpool comeback win - report and player ratings Liverpool 4-3 Villarreal: What Iraola and Ngumoha said Football Daily: Record breaking night as Liverpool, Man City & PSG win - 5 Live reaction The match statistics alone showed what a threat Ngumoha can be.
sentences.article_title: The night 'ruthless' Ngumoha came of age for Liverpool

sentences.text: He had 12 touches in the opposition box, completed seven out of eight dribbles, and registered two crucial assists.
sentences.article_title: The night 'ruthless' Ngumoha came of age for Liverpool

sentences.text: But watching Ngumoha is more than just a numbers experience.
sentences.article_title: The night 'ruthless' Ngumoha came of age for Liverpool

sentences.text: There's a fearless nature to his play that can get the crowd going, and he was the one bright spark in a first half where Liverpool lacked any sort of rhythm.
sentences.article_title: The night 'ruthless' Ngumoha came of age for Liverpool

sentences.text: In a game increasingly focused on structures, Ngumoha's raw ability to take a man on is what helps to set him apart.
sentences.article_title: The night 'ruthless' Ngumoha came of age for Liverpool

sentences.text: "He was magnificent tonight," said former Liverpool forward Daniel Sturridge on Amazon Prime.
sentences.article_title: The night 'ruthless' Ngumoha came of age for Liverpool

sentences.text: "On the ball, this kid has so much potential - and I say 'kid', but he's a young man.
sentences.article_title: The night 'ruthless' Ngumoha came of age for Liverpool

sentences.text: He has so much quality and it's stuff that you can't teach to be honest.
sentences.article_title: The night 'ruthless' Ngumoha came of age for Liverpool

sentences.text: "What he does with the ball at his feet - that is God-given ability - and his hard work on the training pitch, doing things day in and day out, and being ruthless, is what he said in his interview, and I like that.
sentences.article_title: The night 'ruthless' Ngumoha came of age for Liverpool

sentences.text: He wants to be decisive, and I love that." Ngumoha, who has grown up playing down the left, has struggled to get minutes on his preferred side this season, especially with Cody Gakpo and Barcola often playing down that flank.
sentences.article_title: The night 'ruthless' Ngumoha came of age for Liverpool

sentences.text: But head coach Andoni Iraola wants his wingers to be able to play on both sides and Ngumoha's improvement on the right flank has been impressive in such a short space of time.
sentences.article_title: The night 'ruthless' Ngumoha came of age for Liverpool

sentences.text: Ngumoha also spoke about his rapid development on the right on Saturday, after Liverpool beat Brentford.
sentences.article_title: The night 'ruthless' Ngumoha came of age for Liverpool

sentences.text: "I feel like I've got a lot better playing there from the Newcastle game [at the start of this season] until now," Ngumoha said.
sentences.article_title: The night 'ruthless' Ngumoha came of age for Liverpool

sentences.text: "I'm understanding it more.
sentences.article_title: The night 'ruthless' Ngumoha came of age for Liverpool

sentences.text: And going away with England helped a lot as well.
sentences.article_title: The night 'ruthless' Ngumoha came of age for Liverpool

sentences.text: I like playing on both sides.
sentences.article_title: The night 'ruthless' Ngumoha came of age for Liverpool

sentences.text: Janine Lochrenberg was swimming off a beach in KuGompo City (formerly East London) on Tuesday morning when she was attacked.
sentences.article_title: Swimmer, 65, killed in shark attack off South Africa's east coast

sentences.text: Witnesses said the 65-year-old was bitten in two places and died before she was brought to shore.
sentences.article_title: Swimmer, 65, killed in shark attack off South Africa's east coast

sentences.text: Shark attacks are rare in South Africa, with about 10 fatal ones since 2012, according to the Florida Museum's International Shark Attack File.
sentences.article_title: Swimmer, 65, killed in shark attack off South Africa's east coast

sentences.text: Lochrenberg was out on a daily morning swim with her local open water swimming club when she was attacked at around 08:00 (06:00 GMT).
sentences.article_title: Swimmer, 65, killed in shark attack off South Africa's east coast

sentences.text: Fellow swimmers brought her to shore, but it's believed she died before they could get her out of the water.
sentences.article_title: Swimmer, 65, killed in shark attack off South Africa's east coast

sentences.text: She was bitten on her thigh and her upper arm, one of her fellow swimmers told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Swimmer, 65, killed in shark attack off South Africa's east coast

sentences.text: They also said she had been wearing a magnetic shark repellent band on her ankle at the time.
sentences.article_title: Swimmer, 65, killed in shark attack off South Africa's east coast

sentences.text: Lochrenberg's sister Margot said she was holding her sister's head as they brought her to shore but believed she bled out in the water.
sentences.article_title: Swimmer, 65, killed in shark attack off South Africa's east coast

sentences.text: She told the BBC that her sister had "loved the water so much" despite knowing there was an "elevated shark presence in East London".
sentences.article_title: Swimmer, 65, killed in shark attack off South Africa's east coast

sentences.text: "She'd made peace with that.
sentences.article_title: Swimmer, 65, killed in shark attack off South Africa's east coast

sentences.text: She had a deep affinity with the water and was a remarkable person," she said.
sentences.article_title: Swimmer, 65, killed in shark attack off South Africa's east coast

sentences.text: Barbara Briceland, Lochrenberg's partner, told the BBC the retired medical physicist was a good swimmer, who often swam far out into the breakers, and described her as very brave.
sentences.article_title: Swimmer, 65, killed in shark attack off South Africa's east coast

sentences.text: "She was highly intelligent, lots of fun, kind, in a quietish way, thoughtful, well-loved with a love of life." Briceland added they were looking forward to retirement and were about to leave for a three-week road trip together.
sentences.article_title: Swimmer, 65, killed in shark attack off South Africa's east coast

sentences.text: US President Donald Trump is facing another legal challenge on tariffs after the group that successfully sued over his so-called "liberation day" import taxes filed a new lawsuit over the latest Canadian levies.
sentences.article_title: Trump sued over Canadian tariffs in latest legal challenge

sentences.text: The White House imposed a 50% levy on some $20bn of Canadian goods after trade talks between the US and Canada  broke down in August.
sentences.article_title: Trump sued over Canadian tariffs in latest legal challenge

sentences.text: The Liberty Justice Center filed a suit on behalf of US food business Gellert Global Group, urging the US Court of International Trade to find the levies unlawful and to order refunds with interest for affected importers.
sentences.article_title: Trump sued over Canadian tariffs in latest legal challenge

sentences.text: The lawsuit argues the White House exceeded its authority in imposing the tariffs and caused "immediate harm to American businesses".
sentences.article_title: Trump sued over Canadian tariffs in latest legal challenge

sentences.text: The White House has been contacted for comment.
sentences.article_title: Trump sued over Canadian tariffs in latest legal challenge

sentences.text: Gellert Global Group is a third-generation family business that is paying 50% tariffs on cheese exported from Canada.
sentences.article_title: Trump sued over Canadian tariffs in latest legal challenge

sentences.text: The New Jersey-based firm is also facing retaliatory tariffs from Canada on American-made cheese it sells north of the border.
sentences.article_title: Trump sued over Canadian tariffs in latest legal challenge

sentences.text: Co-chief executive Thomas Gellert said the firm had spent generations building relationships with suppliers and customers in the food industry.
sentences.article_title: Trump sued over Canadian tariffs in latest legal challenge

sentences.text: "These tariffs disrupt those relationships overnight and create costs and uncertainty that ripple through the entire supply chain," he said on Tuesday.
sentences.article_title: Trump sued over Canadian tariffs in latest legal challenge

sentences.text: The Liberty Justice Center is challenging the administration's use of Section 338 of the 1930 Tariff Act to hit Canadian goods from wine to dairy products and hockey sticks.
sentences.article_title: Trump sued over Canadian tariffs in latest legal challenge

sentences.text: That section of the nearly 100-year-old Act is aimed at protecting US business against foreign discrimination, but the legal group is arguing that it does not allow the executive branch "to impose sweeping tariffs or import restrictions whenever a trade dispute arises".
sentences.article_title: Trump sued over Canadian tariffs in latest legal challenge

sentences.text: The US-Canada trade war in 5 charts The lawsuit seeks to challenge the White House's reliance on retaliatory tariffs imposed by Canada to justify its own duties under Section 338.
sentences.article_title: Trump sued over Canadian tariffs in latest legal challenge

sentences.text: Canada has imposed a series of countermeasures against numerous US tariffs.
sentences.article_title: Trump sued over Canadian tariffs in latest legal challenge

sentences.text: Last month, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney matched the Section 338 US tariffs "dollar for dollar" after Trump imposed them for what he called "unequal treatment" of US cars, dairy and alcohol.
sentences.article_title: Trump sued over Canadian tariffs in latest legal challenge

sentences.text: It  also points out Section 338 requires a 30-day waiting period before levies can be imposed, but the tariff on products including cheese was added to the list just a week before tariff collection began.
sentences.article_title: Trump sued over Canadian tariffs in latest legal challenge

sentences.text: Sara Albrecht, chief executive of the Liberty Justice Center, said the case was not about Trump himself but about the presidency.
sentences.article_title: Trump sued over Canadian tariffs in latest legal challenge

sentences.text: "No president should have the power to pull a dormant statute off the shelf and use it to impose sweeping tariffs or import bans without the limits Congress required," she said.
sentences.article_title: Trump sued over Canadian tariffs in latest legal challenge

sentences.text: The lawsuit argues that Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 has been superseded by Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974.
sentences.article_title: Trump sued over Canadian tariffs in latest legal challenge

sentences.text: It also argues that if Section 338 still applies, the White House has not established the legal basis for the sweeping tariffs against Canada.
sentences.article_title: Trump sued over Canadian tariffs in latest legal challenge

sentences.text: "The case is not an objection to tariffs as such.
sentences.article_title: Trump sued over Canadian tariffs in latest legal challenge

sentences.text: It asks who has the power to impose them and whether the executive branch followed the law Congress wrote," the Liberty Justice Center said.
sentences.article_title: Trump sued over Canadian tariffs in latest legal challenge

sentences.text: The law group has also filed a motion for a preliminary injunction to block their collection.
sentences.article_title: Trump sued over Canadian tariffs in latest legal challenge

sentences.text: It is the fourth case brought by the group against Trump's tariffs, including its successful case against the sweeping tariffs brought in under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) that were struck down in February this year.
sentences.article_title: Trump sued over Canadian tariffs in latest legal challenge

sentences.text: Albrecht said the group had brought all the cases for the same reason: "the Constitution gives tariff power to Congress.
sentences.article_title: Trump sued over Canadian tariffs in latest legal challenge

sentences.text: The executive branch cannot keep moving the same policy from one statute to another and pretend the limits disappear".
sentences.article_title: Trump sued over Canadian tariffs in latest legal challenge

sentences.text: Fairbarn was seen on CCTV in an elevator on the way to his hotel room with the flamingo A Canadian man has been found guilty of animal cruelty after he took a flamingo from its enclosure in Las Vegas and brought it back to his hotel room during an alcohol-fuelled bender.
sentences.article_title: Tourist found guilty after stealing Las Vegas flamingo from enclosure

sentences.text: Mitchell Fairbarn, who was visiting the US city, took the Chilean flamingo named Peachy from the Flamingo Las Vegas Hotel and Casino in March.
sentences.article_title: Tourist found guilty after stealing Las Vegas flamingo from enclosure

sentences.text: Videos shown at his trial showed a smiling Fairbarn carrying the bird by the neck as he took a lift to his room.
sentences.article_title: Tourist found guilty after stealing Las Vegas flamingo from enclosure

sentences.text: He testified that he had drunk 30 to 40 beers before the incident and said he never meant to harm the animal.
sentences.article_title: Tourist found guilty after stealing Las Vegas flamingo from enclosure

sentences.text: He faces nearly five years in prison.
sentences.article_title: Tourist found guilty after stealing Las Vegas flamingo from enclosure

sentences.text: Animal experts testified the flamingo had feathers torn out and suffered blood loss due to Fairbarn's actions.
sentences.article_title: Tourist found guilty after stealing Las Vegas flamingo from enclosure

sentences.text: A lawyer for Fairbarn said his actions were intended as a harmless prank, and blamed alcohol for his "bad decisions".
sentences.article_title: Tourist found guilty after stealing Las Vegas flamingo from enclosure

sentences.text: "He should not have done that, should not have gone into the habitat, shouldn't have touched a bird, shouldn't have taken Peachy inside," said his lawyer Josh Tomsheck , external .
sentences.article_title: Tourist found guilty after stealing Las Vegas flamingo from enclosure

sentences.text: "The truth is, Mitch was drunk.
sentences.article_title: Tourist found guilty after stealing Las Vegas flamingo from enclosure

sentences.text: He made bad decisions." His lawyer added he had received death threats since his arrest.
sentences.article_title: Tourist found guilty after stealing Las Vegas flamingo from enclosure

sentences.text: Testifying in his defence, Fairbarn, 34, said he thought it would be "funny" to take the bird.
sentences.article_title: Tourist found guilty after stealing Las Vegas flamingo from enclosure

sentences.text: He said he had been up drinking all night and had just gotten off a call with a colleague when he made the decision to abscond with the bird.
sentences.article_title: Tourist found guilty after stealing Las Vegas flamingo from enclosure

sentences.text: The Flamingo Las Vegas, located along the famous Las Vegas strip, features a wildlife habitat inside its hotel and casino that is free to walk through.
sentences.article_title: Tourist found guilty after stealing Las Vegas flamingo from enclosure

sentences.text: It features a flock of Chilean flamingos, other birds, fish and turtles.
sentences.article_title: Tourist found guilty after stealing Las Vegas flamingo from enclosure

sentences.text: During the trial, the jury heard from 14 witnesses and reviewed more than 112 pieces of evidence, according to CBS, the BBC's US partner.
sentences.article_title: Tourist found guilty after stealing Las Vegas flamingo from enclosure

sentences.text: It took a jury around five hours to convict him on felony and misdemeanour animal abuse charges.
sentences.article_title: Tourist found guilty after stealing Las Vegas flamingo from enclosure

sentences.text: Fairbarn has been unable to leave the US since his arrest.
sentences.article_title: Tourist found guilty after stealing Las Vegas flamingo from enclosure

sentences.text: He remains on house arrest in Las Vegas, with a sentencing hearing due to take place in December.
sentences.article_title: Tourist found guilty after stealing Las Vegas flamingo from enclosure

sentences.text: A veterinarian for the state said that Peachy has largely recovered since the event but has a now has a more anxious demeanour around humans.

sentences.text: El Mansouri (left) was named by King Mohammed VI (right) as the country's first female prime minister The Islamic saying "a people who entrust their affairs to a woman will never succeed" has resurfaced in Morocco since King Mohammed VI named Fatima Zahra El Mansouri as the country's first female prime minister.

sentences.text: He argued that Morocco, a Muslim majority country, had found a balance between equality and the responsibilities of state leadership, as the highest office - that of the king - continued to be reserved for men.

sentences.text: Morocco operates as a constitutional monarchy.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: The day after her appointment, local broadcaster Chouf TV took to the streets to ask Moroccan men "what they thought" of a woman heading the government.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: Several men, mostly middle-aged or older, hesitated before answering.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: Some said they accepted the decision because it was the king's choice.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: One grey-haired man, who did not give his name or age, said: "It feels strange to have a woman as head of government.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: I'm not sure if it sits well with me." Criticism of the monarchy carries legal risks in Morocco.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: The penal code criminalises certain forms of offence or insult against the king, the royal family and the monarchy.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: Online, the appointment became fodder for political satire.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: A video showing two women pulling each other's hair was widely shared, with captions suggesting that this is what parliamentary disagreements between El Mansouri and her colleagues might look like.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: However many younger Moroccans, especially women, welcomed her appointment.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: While attitudes are changing in Morocco, conservative, religious views still hold great weight.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: Some of the country's most contentious debates over gender equality centre on family law, including inheritance, marriage and divorce.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: Under existing inheritance rules, a daughter typically receives half the share of a son in comparable circumstances.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: The Higher Council of Ulemas, the country's body of religious scholars, has resisted calls for equal inheritance, citing Islamic jurisprudence.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: It has also rejected proposals to abolish taasib, a rule that can require female orphans without brothers to share their inheritance with male relatives, including distant ones.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: In a 2022 report, Morocco's National Human Rights Council said unequal inheritance rules contributed to poverty among women.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: Polygamy is also legal under certain conditions.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: But exceptions remain, including provisions relating to a first wife's infertility or illness, which women's rights groups have criticised on grounds of privacy and medical confidentiality.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: El Mansouri is no newcomer to politics.
sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: "The latter cannot be understood without the former." Official figures put turnout at just 38% of registered voters, while the proportion of all eligible voters who cast a ballot was even lower.

sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: She argues that promoting a woman to the highest government office might be intended to project an image of modernisation and progress, even when the political system and the pace of social reform remain largely unchanged.

sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.article_title: Morocco's first female prime minister caught between the king, clerics, and feminists

sentences.text: "I don't think El Mansouri should be judged by the fact that she is a woman.
