sentences.text: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence Warning: this article contains discussion of eating disorders "If you keep this up, you'll be in a wheelchair at 30." That is what doctors told British long-distance runner Jake Smith four years ago.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: From the outside looking in, his career was flying.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: By the age of 23, he had signed a professional contract with Nike and represented Great Britain on the global stage.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: But at the same time, his body was deteriorating - enduring a relentless pattern of race, illness, injury, repeat.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: Balancing an intense training regime with disordered eating meant the 28-year-old returned from a running camp in Uganda weighing just eight stone (51kg) at 5ft 5in (1.7m).
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: He had such brittle bones that he was told his career could be over.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: After suffering two stress fractures in the space of four months, Smith sought professional help and was diagnosed with REDs – relative energy deficiency in sport.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: It is a syndrome that can affect anyone and if left undiagnosed or untreated, can have an impact on performance and cause serious, long-lasting health problems.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: The symptoms are slightly better documented in women - just last month, tennis player Emma Navarro revealed her diagnosis and subsequent decision to step away from competition until 2027.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: But men are just as susceptible and due to stigma and lack of obvious warning signs, it can go undetected for longer and means many, like Smith, suffer in silence.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: BBC Sport explains what the condition is, how it affects men and women and why, despite its prevalence and severity, REDs remains a relatively under-reported and overlooked area of sports science.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: REDs can cause bone stress injuries, disrupted sleep, fatigue and low mood.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: Left untreated, the condition can lead to serious long-term health problems, including osteoporosis, cardiovascular disease and fertility issues.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: Dr Nicky Keay, an expert in hormone health, says many of these symptoms stem from hormonal disruption caused by insufficient energy intake.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: "Hormones go to every single bit in your body.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: So, if your hormones are not working well for you, you're going to feel it in all sorts of different areas," she says.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: "In order to have healthy hormones, they need to be fed regularly.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: If you're not doing that and there's an energy deficit, often some of those hormone systems will slow down or shut down completely." Women have a monthly barometer of their hormone health with the menstrual cycle, described by Keay as a "free monthly medical check".
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: Put simply, she says, a woman suffering from REDs can have her periods "switched off".
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: For men, it is more subtle – testosterone levels will drop, resulting in a reduced libido and fatigue.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: The impact on a woman's period is why the condition was first referred to in the early 1990s as the "female athlete triad".
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: But it was renamed by the International Olympic Committee in 2014 to acknowledge the broader range of symptoms of energy deficiency and that it also harms male athletes.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: "We realised we were ignoring the other half of the population," Keay says.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: "It's a strange situation because normally it's women's health that is the one being ignored but, in this situation, it's the men who weren't being recognised or represented." Twelve years later that decision appears to be vindicated, with recent research highlighting the prevalence in men.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: Meta-analysis published in Australian journal Sports Medicine last year, following a study involving thousands of elite and amateur athletes around the world, indicated  44.2% of female athletes and 49.4% of male athletes had low energy availability.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: Jake Smith was regularly getting injured So why is REDs so common?
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: One of the answers lies in the phrase 'lighter is faster'.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: For decades, it had been an accepted wisdom in sports like endurance running, cycling, climbing, horse riding, dancing and aesthetic sports like diving and gymnastics.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: And for athletes like Smith, it is how his problems started.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: "I believed it for years.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: I thought that was the way forward," he says.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: "I started thinking 'how do I improve my half marathon by 10 seconds?
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: Is it a drop in weight?'.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: And that's when my head completely went." Initially, the strategy can work.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: When it comes to choosing energy to cover training demand or energy to stay healthy, the body has learned through evolution and threat of predators to always prioritise movement.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: It means that athletes can drop weight and still train and exercise and achieve good results.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: But eventually, the luck runs out.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: Described by Keay as "fool's gold", the body will adjust to the energy deficit and cause a drop in performance and high risk of injuries.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: This video can not be played The athletes affected by relative energy deficiency in sport Olympic and world champion Jonny Brownlee acknowledges under-fuelling mistakes he made in his triathlon career contributed to serious injuries.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: "I didn't see the importance of it.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: Training came first and I think we weren't educated enough in how important fuelling was," he tells BBC Sport.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: "You were seen, culturally, as a bit weak if you were fuelling on the bike.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: And the impact of that was definitely injuries - probably not recovering from my training quite as well as I should have done, stress responses, stress fractures.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: So there's that side of it and probably underperformance in races as well." Brownlee, who recently announced his retirement, believes the culture of not fuelling on the bike has now changed but a stigma lingers around REDs and the perception that it is a "female issue".
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: "In females, there are more obvious signs but in males it can go under the radar a little bit and then it hits you by a really serious injury," he says.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: "I think there's a stigma attached in there, or it's not looked at as the obvious answer to some of your problems, it's found later down the line.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: Men also don't like to talk about under-fuelling because it's just seen as 'you probably should feel better and you should be on top of that'." It is those attitudes among male athletes that prompted Keay to conduct an experiment in 2019.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: Assessing 50 male competitive cyclists, Keay found in her initial screenings that nearly half had poor bone health and 25% were suffering from REDs.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: The cyclists were then split into two groups and across a six-month period, one half continued their training and fuelling habits as before while the others were tutored by Keay and offered nutrition and training advice.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: "The group that I left to their own devices unfortunately went on the default and they lost even more bone mineral density, similar to an astronaut in space… And they performed OK, but relative to their functional threshold power, they didn't get the race results that you would have expected.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: "For the group I took under my wing, there was an improvement in their bone health and really good race results.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: "So, I had evidence that REDs definitely does exist quite extensively in my group of the male cyclists and you're going to underperform if you don't fuel sufficiently.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: The good news is that REDs is reversible.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: But if you don't take action, it's a decline." Jonny Brownlee is a three-time Olympic medallist As the syndrome and its symptoms are still not commonly known, it is often difficult to know where to find help.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: After former GB runner Pippa Woolven's struggles with the condition, she set up a website called Project REDs which offers information and practical resources for athletes, coaches, parents and healthcare professionals.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: Keay also helps people competing at all levels to recover from REDs.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: Most of her patients are women, but she is starting to see more men reach out for help who, she says, are often in "bad shape".
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: "I think the men are maybe more reluctant than the women, or maybe they don't realise they've got it.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: Sometimes they might use a different word for it, they say burnout," Keay says.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: "I don't mind that though because there is definitely a psychological aspect to REDs.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: Why are you not eating the carbohydrates?" Sometimes, it's hard to answer those questions because the under-fuelling is unintentional, either from not understanding or underestimating energy requirements or failing to match an increase in the intensity or duration of exercise with higher calorie or carbohydrate intake.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: For others, former British cycling champion Brian Smith among them, the answer comes from intention.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: "I always felt like I was overweight.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: Everybody was under pressure regarding weight, but nobody really spoke about it," he says.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: "I'm just under six foot and I've got large glutes and thigh muscles.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: As a road cyclist, I used to race at 68kg and for my height and build, that's quite skinny.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: I even got down to about 66kg and when I got down to that, I felt underpowered, I felt bad." Smith, now 59, only discovered he had been suffering from REDs during his career when he started running eight years ago and developed three severe stress fractures, including one in his femur.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: Such has been the toll on his body that Smith says he would now never encourage anyone to pursue a career as a professional cyclist.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: "It really is not healthy," he says.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: "If you want to go to the highest levels of the sport, you will suffer later on in life.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: You're destroying your body.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: "Sporting teams don't care - all they're worried about is performance.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: So they will nurture a rider, they will feed a rider, they'll get a rider to be a certain weight.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: They don't care about what happens to them later in life.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: "I'm suffering now and I've so many regrets.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: I just wish I'd known more about this." While Smith believes his sport has a long way to go in changing attitudes, British Cycling says a lot of progress has been made through education that starts at academy level and annual physical and psychological screenings.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: "One of the big things we've done in the past 10 years is try and turn this into a performance-related conversation," Dr Nigel Jones, British Cycling chief medical officer, tells BBC Sport.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: "Now, we couch the conversation with an athlete around 'if you under-fuel, you will not be able to perform at your best', whereas previously, conversations in power-to-weight ratio sports might have been 'you need to be lighter'.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: "I think it would be naive to say REDs is never going to be an issue.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: But I would like to believe that its prevalence will reduce with the work that we're doing," he adds.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: World Climbing has mandatory health checks on its athletes to combat REDs British Cycling is not alone in this approach, with World Climbing taking things a step further two years ago with the introduction of mandatory health checks on athletes.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: The policy was drawn up by expert Professor Naama Constantini, who says she is "proud" of the move by World Climbing and believes other federations should follow suit.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: "We are trying to educate and prevent.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: I'm not a policeman and we're not looking for cheaters.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: I'm a medical doctor and we want to make sure our athletes are healthy," she says.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: "Prevention is the best medicine you can give.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: We want athletes and coaches to understand that it's not about weight.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: It's about strength, it's about performance and fuelling the body and you pay a price if you lose weight in an unhealthy way." With more awareness and education, it is hoped the tide can be turned on REDs.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: But many still suffer in ignorance, as well as silence.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: That is what motivates Jake Smith to keep sharing his recovery on social media, with hundreds of men and women messaging him for advice and support.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: Smith has managed to reverse his condition and is now racing better than ever, recently completing the Berlin marathon in a personal-best time of two hours, nine minutes and 24 seconds.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: The big goal is the 2028 Olympics, but he is adamant that the priority is making sure he stands on every start line as healthy as possible.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: "I'd never want to see an athlete go through the years I've had.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: I'm 10-15 kilos heavier than I've ever been and the biggest thing I can say is I've never been so happy.
sentences.article_title: Race, illness, injury, repeat - REDs and why men are suffering in silence

sentences.text: Despite its enormous size, the fast-swimming creature is elusive and spends much of its life in the open ocean and often surfacing only briefly before disappearing beneath the waves.

sentences.text: The mammal can be found all over the world's oceans but is most at home in cooler waters.

sentences.text: Crime scene evidence is often not enough to identify suspects Randy Gail Sperino was last seen alive on the evening of 9 November 1993, as she was getting into a pickup truck in Granite City, Illinois.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: The 34-year-old's body was found hours later in a field nearby, the victim of blunt force trauma.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: The identity of her killer was a mystery.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: DNA evidence found at the crime scene was tested against standard law enforcement databases, but no matches were found.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: For three decades, investigators from the Madison County Sheriff's Office chased leads and interviewed hundreds of people as they attempted to identify the perpetrator.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: The case looked like it would remain one of more than 250,000 unsolved homicides in the US.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: Then, last year, detectives tried a fresh approach.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: They sent genetic evidence to Othram, a Houston-based company that uses DNA technology to help identify the perpetrators in cold and current crime cases.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: The Madison County detectives had been inspired by investigative genetic genealogy techniques used to identify the Golden State Killer, Joseph James DeAngelo, back in 2018.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: In that case, an investigative team constructed a family tree to help identify the killer.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: They were able to do so thanks to DNA data that relatives had provided to commercial databases, similar to consumer ancestry platforms.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: Unlike traditional forensic DNA testing, which generally relies on a direct comparison between evidence and a known person, investigative genetic genealogy can identify distant genetic relatives of an unknown individual.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: Othram set about applying this technique to track down Sperino's killer.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: While the killer's own DNA profile wasn't available, profiles submitted by his extended relatives allowed the company to identify a male family member.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: "That lead broke the case open," said Captain Tim Lawrence of Madison County Sheriff's Office, which was responsible for investigating the crime.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: It was a crucial clue that led the detectives to Albert "Buddy" Zigler, 70, who then confessed to the murder.

sentences.text: He was charged in May this year.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: The Unite union has hit out at a plan by NatWest to reduce the rights of 30,000 of its employees to work from home.

sentences.text: NatWest says it is moving to a hybrid approach where workers will be required to attend the office at least two days a week, from February.

sentences.article_title: Union attacks NatWest plans to get workers back to the office

sentences.text: But Unite said NatWest's decision was "out of touch with the realities facing its workforce", with many facing higher travel and childcare costs.
sentences.article_title: Union attacks NatWest plans to get workers back to the office

sentences.article_title: Union attacks NatWest plans to get workers back to the office

sentences.text: In January last year, Amazon required staff to return to the office five days a week after they had been working two days at home.
sentences.article_title: Union attacks NatWest plans to get workers back to the office

sentences.text: Other firms such as Boots and JP Morgan have brought in policies requiring head office staff to be in every day.
sentences.article_title: Union attacks NatWest plans to get workers back to the office

sentences.text: But Barclays faced a backlash from staff last month over plans to require workers to go to the office three days a week.
sentences.article_title: Union attacks NatWest plans to get workers back to the office

sentences.article_title: Union attacks NatWest plans to get workers back to the office

sentences.text: Both Queen's University Belfast and Ulster University are expected to have financial deficits in 2025/26 Northern Ireland's universities are facing a "substantial" cut of £21m in the Stormont funding they receive to teach students.
sentences.article_title: Universities face 'substantial' funding cuts amid budget delay

sentences.text: The top official at the Department for the Economy (DfE), Ian Snowden, said the universities were facing a reduction of 6% on the opening funding they received in 2024/25.
sentences.article_title: Universities face 'substantial' funding cuts amid budget delay

sentences.text: The potential cuts come as the Northern Ireland Executive remains seven months into the financial year without a budget.
sentences.article_title: Universities face 'substantial' funding cuts amid budget delay

sentences.text: Snowden said both Queen's University Belfast (QUB) and Ulster University (UU) are expected to have financial deficits in 2025/26.
sentences.article_title: Universities face 'substantial' funding cuts amid budget delay

sentences.text: With no agreed budget for 2025/26, Stormont departments have been operating under contingency arrangements allowing them to spend up to 95% of last year's funding.
sentences.article_title: Universities face 'substantial' funding cuts amid budget delay

sentences.text: The DfE is the Stormont department with responsibility for higher and further education in Northern Ireland.
sentences.article_title: Universities face 'substantial' funding cuts amid budget delay

sentences.text: Universities are mainly funded through student fees and a "teaching grant" provided by DfE.
sentences.article_title: Universities face 'substantial' funding cuts amid budget delay

sentences.text: Further education colleges have already announced big cuts to student places and courses.
sentences.article_title: Universities face 'substantial' funding cuts amid budget delay

sentences.text: Ulster University, meanwhile, is making 450 staff redundant across its campuses to save about £25m.
sentences.article_title: Universities face 'substantial' funding cuts amid budget delay

sentences.text: The chair of Stormont's economy committee, Democratic Unionist Party assembly member Phillip Brett, said a further cut in university funding could mean that the universities would not receive money for three months for students they have already enrolled.
sentences.article_title: Universities face 'substantial' funding cuts amid budget delay

sentences.text: "The universities have taken students on in the anticipation that they will receive funding from the department," he said.
sentences.article_title: Universities face 'substantial' funding cuts amid budget delay

sentences.text: "We're now six months into the financial year and they still haven't received a formal letter of offer from the department.
sentences.article_title: Universities face 'substantial' funding cuts amid budget delay

sentences.text: "And despite students enrolling in September, one of the contingencies from the department is now that come January, February, March you might say 'actually we're not going to pay you for these three months of the students that you've taken on'?" "It's a possibility," Snowden told the committee.
sentences.article_title: Universities face 'substantial' funding cuts amid budget delay

sentences.text: He also said the universities could only get confirmation of how much funding they would get when the executive agreed a budget.
sentences.article_title: Universities face 'substantial' funding cuts amid budget delay

sentences.text: "At this point we still don't know how much money we have to spend," he said.
sentences.article_title: Universities face 'substantial' funding cuts amid budget delay

sentences.text: Amy Smith is the president of the National Union of Students-Union of Students in Ireland Amy Smith, the National Union of Students-Union of Students in Ireland (NUS-USI) president, said it was "disappointing to hear that our universities will be facing cuts to their teaching grants".
sentences.article_title: Universities face 'substantial' funding cuts amid budget delay

sentences.text: "Any cuts directly impact students, their access to their education and the quality of the experience they receive while at university costs to them remain the same," she added.
sentences.article_title: Universities face 'substantial' funding cuts amid budget delay

sentences.text: "Students and staff must not be left to shoulder the cost of underfunding.
sentences.article_title: Universities face 'substantial' funding cuts amid budget delay

sentences.text: "We continue to work constructively with the Department for the Economy and government partners to secure a long-term solution that will benefit students and the wider economy," they said.
sentences.article_title: Universities face 'substantial' funding cuts amid budget delay

sentences.text: "Given the deteriorating funding situation from the department, which we regard as very serious, we will continue to enact appropriate caution in relation to our finances," the spokesperson said.
sentences.article_title: Universities face 'substantial' funding cuts amid budget delay

sentences.text: They also said 735 university staff had applied for voluntary redundancy.
sentences.article_title: Universities face 'substantial' funding cuts amid budget delay

sentences.text: OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman has won a dismissal of a lawsuit brought against him by his sister that claimed he had sexually abused her more than two decades ago.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman wins dismissal of sister's lawsuit

sentences.text: A US district judge dismissed the case after Ann Altman had refused to attend an independent medical examination, adding she was warned a failure to do so would result in the case being thrown out.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman wins dismissal of sister's lawsuit

sentences.text: Ann Altman had claimed the OpenAI founder had regularly sexually abused her between 1997 and 2006.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman wins dismissal of sister's lawsuit

sentences.text: Sam Altman has denied those accusations.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman wins dismissal of sister's lawsuit

sentences.text: The Altman family has said Ann Altman has mental health challenges and they have supported her financially, adding the claims were made as she continued to demand more funds.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman wins dismissal of sister's lawsuit

sentences.text: District Judge Zachary Bluestone said that despite multiple accommodations and multiple opportunities to do so, Ann Altman did not appear for an independent medical exam on three separate occasions, and "failed to meaningfully prosecute her case".
sentences.article_title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman wins dismissal of sister's lawsuit

sentences.text: "Because Annie has continued to violate her discovery obligations and forced this case to a halt through her intransigence, the Court has run out of options and, thus, dismisses her claims with prejudice," he said in his written order.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman wins dismissal of sister's lawsuit

sentences.text: The case was filed on 6 January 2025 in the Eastern District of Missouri.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman wins dismissal of sister's lawsuit

sentences.text: In it, Ann Altman claimed that her older brother Sam Altman began abusing her when she was three, and he was 12.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman wins dismissal of sister's lawsuit

sentences.text: However, in a joint statement released by Sam Altman along with his mother and two brothers at the time, the family said they were concerned for Ann Altman's wellbeing and have spent years trying to support her financially and to look after her wellbeing.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman wins dismissal of sister's lawsuit

sentences.text: The family said she receives monthly financial support, and her bills and rent were also covered, while also trying to assist with medical help.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman wins dismissal of sister's lawsuit

sentences.text: The statement said her claims against Sam Altman had changed drastically over time, but all of those claims were "utterly untrue".
sentences.article_title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman wins dismissal of sister's lawsuit

sentences.text: The UK's unemployment rate has dropped to its lowest for more than year, but job vacancies have continued to fall as smaller businesses cut back on recruitment, official figures indicate.
sentences.article_title: Jobless rate falls but small firms cut back hiring

sentences.text: The jobless rate fell to 4.7% in the three months to August, the Office for National Statistics (ONS) said, the lowest since July last year.

sentences.text: The US has ordered all artificial intelligence (AI) technology from the Chinese firm DeepSeek to be removed from most government systems.
sentences.article_title: US bans China's DeepSeek from government in race for AI dominance

sentences.text: The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has banned all use of DeepSeek within civilian government agencies, and any technology built with the aid of its AI models.
sentences.article_title: US bans China's DeepSeek from government in race for AI dominance

sentences.text: As a powerful AI model that is open source - meaning it is free to access and less expensive to use - DeepSeek has been seen as a disruptive force in the ongoing AI technology race.
sentences.article_title: US bans China's DeepSeek from government in race for AI dominance

sentences.text: While the DHS notice did not detail the exact security concerns surrounding DeepSeek, the White House has this year criticised AI firms from China.
sentences.article_title: US bans China's DeepSeek from government in race for AI dominance

sentences.text: The DHS, DeepSeek, and the Chinese embassy in Washington DC have been contacted for comment.
sentences.article_title: US bans China's DeepSeek from government in race for AI dominance

sentences.text: The DHS made the order public on Monday, but the ban took effect from the end of July.
sentences.article_title: US bans China's DeepSeek from government in race for AI dominance

sentences.text: The order is specific to civilian agencies, including the Department of the Treasury, the Department of State and the Department of Justice.
sentences.article_title: US bans China's DeepSeek from government in race for AI dominance

sentences.text: However, agencies within the Department of Defense are excluded.
sentences.article_title: US bans China's DeepSeek from government in race for AI dominance

sentences.text: The ban follows criticism of Chinese AI from the Trump administration, and from American firms.
sentences.article_title: US bans China's DeepSeek from government in race for AI dominance

sentences.text: White House tech lead Michael Kratsios wrote earlier this year in an internal memo that "malicious exploitation" of American AI firms had been occurring, mainly by rival firms in China.
sentences.article_title: US bans China's DeepSeek from government in race for AI dominance

sentences.text: Anthropic and OpenAI, both of which are poised to list on the public stock market in the coming months, have also claimed to have had their AI models essentially copied by some Chinese AI firms, including DeepSeek.

sentences.text: US president Donald Trump has made clear that he sees China as the key US rival when it comes to development of AI, something he sees as crucial to the future of the country.
sentences.article_title: US bans China's DeepSeek from government in race for AI dominance

sentences.text: DeepSeek has grown in popularity since its initial public release in 2025, with models being in such demand that the company's servers have gone down at times.
sentences.article_title: US bans China's DeepSeek from government in race for AI dominance

sentences.article_title: US bans China's DeepSeek from government in race for AI dominance

sentences.article_title: US bans China's DeepSeek from government in race for AI dominance

sentences.text: For a technology or AI developer, using DeepSeek in their work costs a fraction of what a closed model like Google's Google's Gemini, Anthropic's Claude or OpenAI's Codex would.

sentences.article_title: US bans China's DeepSeek from government in race for AI dominance

sentences.text: Chancellor John Healey will set out Labour's tax and spending plans when he delivers his first Budget on 28 October.
sentences.article_title: What is the Budget and what could be in it?

sentences.text: He has refused to rule out tax increases after acknowledging government borrowing costs are at "historic highs".
sentences.article_title: What is the Budget and what could be in it?

sentences.text: But the government's room for manoeuvre on tax is limited.
sentences.article_title: What is the Budget and what could be in it?

sentences.text: Before the 2024 general election, Labour promised not to increase three big revenue earners for the government: income tax, National Insurance and VAT.
sentences.article_title: What is the Budget and what could be in it?

sentences.text: In his statement, delivered to MPs in the House of Commons, Healey will set out how the government plans to raise or lower taxes.
sentences.article_title: What is the Budget and what could be in it?

sentences.text: Alongside the Budget, the Treasury will publish details about the measures and their costs.
sentences.article_title: What is the Budget and what could be in it?

sentences.text: The independent Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR), which monitors government spending, will also publish an assessment of the health of the UK economy and a forecast of what it thinks will happen in the future.
sentences.article_title: What is the Budget and what could be in it?

sentences.text: The run-up to the Budget typically generates speculation about what might be in it,  which the government is trying to keep to a minimum this year.
sentences.article_title: What is the Budget and what could be in it?

sentences.text: Healey and Prime Minister Andy Burnham face a difficult balancing act, trying to offer more support to households and meet commitments on defence spending,  while also sticking to Labour's manifesto commitments on tax and the government's self-imposed fiscal rules.
sentences.article_title: What is the Budget and what could be in it?

sentences.text: The previous chancellor, Rachel Reeves, set out two main rules, which the new leadership has vowed to follow.
sentences.article_title: What is the Budget and what could be in it?

sentences.text: These are: Not to borrow to fund day-to-day public spending by the end of this parliament To get government debt falling as a share of national income by the end of this parliament In March, the OBR calculated that the first rule would be met with a gap - or headroom - of £23.6bn.
sentences.article_title: What is the Budget and what could be in it?

sentences.text: However, this headroom is expected to have shrunk.
sentences.article_title: What is the Budget and what could be in it?

sentences.text: Analysts are divided on how much it may have fallen by.
sentences.article_title: What is the Budget and what could be in it?

sentences.text: While a rise in government borrowing costs will increase debt interest payments, higher inflation could push up tax revenues.
sentences.article_title: What is the Budget and what could be in it?

sentences.article_title: What is the Budget and what could be in it?

sentences.text: Drivers will be given the right to challenge "rip-off" private parking charges and more grace when using private providers under new rules set out by Andy Burnham.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows end to 'rip-off parking charges' under new rules

sentences.text: The prime minister announced the changes after concerns were raised that penalties issued by private providers were too harsh and left motorists unfairly punished.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows end to 'rip-off parking charges' under new rules

sentences.text: The new rules include a cancellation of charges for honest mistakes such as stopping to check directions and for non-payment due to broken ticket machines.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows end to 'rip-off parking charges' under new rules

sentences.text: Drivers will also get a 10-minute window to leave a car park without facing a penalty.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows end to 'rip-off parking charges' under new rules

sentences.text: Motoring groups welcomed the changes, but said more needed to be done to stop charges when the driver had done nothing wrong.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows end to 'rip-off parking charges' under new rules

sentences.text: Private car parks are different to council-owned car parks and streets, but more tickets at private sites are now being issued than ever recorded.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows end to 'rip-off parking charges' under new rules

sentences.text: According to RAC analysis of government data, some 17 million private parking tickets were issued in 2025-26, a 17% increase from a year earlier.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows end to 'rip-off parking charges' under new rules

sentences.text: With each charge worth up to £100, the data suggests drivers could collectively face private parking charges worth more than £4.6m each day.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows end to 'rip-off parking charges' under new rules

sentences.text: In one case, a woman was taken to court in a £1,906 claim after taking longer than five minutes to pay at a car park in Derby .
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows end to 'rip-off parking charges' under new rules

sentences.text: The charge was eventually dropped .
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows end to 'rip-off parking charges' under new rules

sentences.text: "Being a few minutes late back to your car or typing one digit of your number plate wrong shouldn't end with a hefty fine landing on your doormat," said Burnham.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows end to 'rip-off parking charges' under new rules

sentences.text: He added that such charges left "people feeling ripped off and out of pocket".
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows end to 'rip-off parking charges' under new rules

sentences.text: In 2019, an act of Parliament was passed to create a code but the code was withdrawn in 2022, due to "resistance from the private parking industry", according to the RAC.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows end to 'rip-off parking charges' under new rules

sentences.text: The current industry Code of Practice, created by the British Parking Association and the International Parking Community, was introduced in 2024 and updated last year after a review .
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows end to 'rip-off parking charges' under new rules

sentences.text: Angela Rayner, the Communities and Housing Secretary, told BBC Breakfast that parking "shouldn't be a way of making money".
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows end to 'rip-off parking charges' under new rules

sentences.text: Asked if the changes were an admission that motorists have been "ripped off" by parking companies for years, she said: "We're calling time on it.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows end to 'rip-off parking charges' under new rules

sentences.text: They have regulated themselves and they have their appeals process but we're giving it more meat now." She said the current level of fine was a "proportionate response to when people don't follow the rules".
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows end to 'rip-off parking charges' under new rules

sentences.text: Derek Millard-Smith from the British Parking Association said the group welcomed the changes as it would "increase trust" and said "detterents work" when it came to questions over the cost of fines.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows end to 'rip-off parking charges' under new rules

sentences.text: "We know dog fouling, rail fare dodging, littering - all those levels are around £100 or more because that is a level that is deemed sufficient to change behaviours." Both the AA and the RAC said the new code was a good first step but did not go far enough.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows end to 'rip-off parking charges' under new rules

sentences.text: The AA said some drivers pay up even if they have done nothing wrong, just to avoid the hassle and over fears of legal action being taken against them.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows end to 'rip-off parking charges' under new rules

sentences.text: "There is still a huge amount of work to do, such as tackling the scourge of debt recovery fees," added Jack Cousens, head of roads policy at the AA.

sentences.text: "Ultimately, we need to stop charges being issued in the first place, especially where the driver has done nothing wrong." sentences.text: The government said it would be consulting on the issue of debt recovery fees, as well as other recommendations from the Competition and Markets Authority.

sentences.text: Bereaved families affected by severe delays paying out civil service pensions could face an "unjust" tax bill, the government has been warned.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: Under HMRC rules, certain lump sum pension payments must be paid within two years of the pension scheme being notified of a death to remain tax-free.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: Conservative MP Sir Geoffrey Clifton-Brown, who chairs Parliament's Public Accounts Committee, said it was "unconscionable" some families could face a "death tax" through no fault of their own.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: The Cabinet Office said that if delays caused a tax charge there were existing avenues to claim compensation, such as the Pensions Ombudsman.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: However, the ombudsman is currently advising that standard complaints are only likely to be resolved within 18 months, with more complex cases facing a longer wait.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: The Civil Service Pension scheme manages the pensions of 1.7 million public sector workers in the UK.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: Outsourcing firm Capita took over the administration of the scheme from a company called MyCSP in December 2025, saying it inherited a backlog of more than 86,000 cases.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: Despite a two-year transition period to prepare for the takeover, problems have persisted and by February the backlog had grown to 120,000 cases.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: Retired civil servants and bereaved families have been left waiting months for pension payments, with some struggling to pay bills.

sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.article_title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays

sentences.text: "The units for dosages and blood tests often include Greek letters," says Carol Bereuter, who is a specialist in medical translations.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: She came across one automatically-translated text that had translated the greek letter μ as milli (one thousandth) instead of micro (one millionth).
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: If you give someone a milligram when it's meant to be a microgram, you are giving them a thousand times the dose," points out Bereuter.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: She also makes the point that, as AI translators have got better, catching errors has got more difficult.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: "Whereas in the past, with things like Google Translate, the sentence would jump out at you because there'd be a grammatical error or it would sound clunky, today it sounds perfectly legitimate.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: So the errors are a lot harder to spot." Carol Bereuter is a specialist in medical translations "If it's something that will bear your signature, there's a risk for your reputation.

sentences.text: And if decisions are going to be taken on the basis of a translation concerning a medical procedure, a contract you might sign or a major purchase you might make, the risk is even greater," warns François Yvon.

sentences.text: Even sentences that seem quite clear to a human can trip up an AI service, he says.
sentences.article_title: How long will humans be needed for translation?

sentences.text: "When you have words with different meanings, it's usually very clear for a human which one applies because they understand the context, but when a machine translator comes across the sentence 'translate into Polish', for example, it is quite capable of deciding it must be all about shoe cream, says Yvon.

sentences.text: Context is often crucial.

sentences.text: "27% of the AI-generated text still got corrected before publication.

sentences.text: Eradicating those errors is likely to be challenging.

sentences.text: "As things stand, I think the fundamental way these systems function makes it quite hard to imagine how they could become 100% reliable," says François Yvon.

But perhaps the big moment will be when AI can show doubt.

sentences.text: The operators of Newby Island landfill have been ordered to take action over odours Milpitas, an affluent city in California's Silicon Valley tech hub, has an odour problem.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: For decades, residents have had to endure rank smells wafting from industrial sites, among them a 342-acre landfill.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "When I first moved here, I could not open my window for over 10 years," says Chia-Ling Kong, an engineer for a tech firm who lives around half a mile from the dump.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: While things have got better in recent years, Kong says she and her neighbours must still contend with around "two or three hours of bad smells a day".
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Perhaps befitting Silicon Valley, the community is putting its hopes in technology.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: The operators of Newby Island landfill have been ordered by local authorities to use drones and install monitors to systematically track and measure the chemicals responsible for bad odours.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: They have also been told to automate the collection of landfill gases responsible for smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Kong is optimistic a data-driven approach will make a difference.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "Hopefully with this continuous monitoring, it makes it easier to pinpoint problems at the moment it starts." The operators of the landfill say they are committed to operating it safely and protecting air quality.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Just like in Milpitas, where Kong is part of a citizen's campaign against the odours, communities around the world are raising a stink about bad smells making day-to-day life miserable.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Sometimes a rubbish dump is to blame, or it might be a sewage treatment works, or a reeking factory.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: When the complaints start stacking up, resolving them is not always simple.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Many countries have no regulations in place dictating how to manage smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: In the US, for example, the Environmental Protection Agency does not regulate environmental odours as a pollutant.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: This leaves states and local governments to take charge of the issue.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Urban sprawl is often part of the problem, bringing communities closer to stinky facilities that may historically have been kept at a distance.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: This is creating more demand for technologies to monitor and prevent smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Odour consultant Micheal Bull says people are increasingly concerned about neighbourhood stinks.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "You're getting developments being built nearer to odorous processes… as land has become more valuable, there is also infilling," Bull says.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: He is speaking about his experiences in the UK, but it's a similar story in many parts of the world.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Bad smells from waste sites are among the most difficult to resolve The technologies used to tackle industrial pongs generally fall into three categories: they absorb odours; convert them into something less smelly through a chemical reaction; or burn them away.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Experts on fixing industrial odours say that the best technologies, when used correctly, can remove 90% or more of the target compounds responsible for smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: But this can be expensive and some operators opt for simpler and cheaper solutions.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: These include masking odours from landfill or sewage processing by spraying giant quantities of deodorisers.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Odour experts contacted for this article were dubious about the effectiveness of such industrial scale air fresheners.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "In my view they're not likely to change the odours," says Bull, who likens them to fabric conditioner.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Bad smells from waste sites – a common cause of complaints – are among the stinkiest and most difficult to resolve, according to Carlos Diaz, an environmental consultant based in Spain.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "Landfill is difficult to treat because you have a very large surface," he says.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: In some places at least, technology is making a real difference.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Residents in Des Moines, Iowa, have long complained of the so-called Eastside Funk, a putrid scent that residents report drifts over parts of the city.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: A study commissioned by city authorities showed that a trio of industrial meat companies were among culprits.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "Within 10 miles, there's about half a million people," says Dalton Jacobus, who works in the Department of Neighborhood Services.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "If the winds are out of the wrong direction, 100,000 people can be in the middle of that odour plume." The authorities are now paying around $240,000 (£182,000) a year on technology to track the stink, so they can take action.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "What we wanted to do was build a ring of odour monitors around the facilities that we suspected of emitting odours," says Jacobus.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: The monitors, which measure levels of chemical compounds in the air, work in combination with a weather station to provide real-time data on the concentrations that are coming from each facility based off the wind patterns.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: This has put an end to finger pointing about who's to blame each time a smell sparks complaints, says Jacobus.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Smithfield Foods, which operates a meat processing in Des Moines, says it has invested $2m to install a regenerative thermal oxidiser that destroys the chemicals associated with bad smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Even so, the company says it does not believe it is the source of odour complaints.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Before installing the monitors – which some local companies help pay for – officials in Des Moines would drive out to the source of a complaint to sniff the air.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Relying on the human nose to sniff out industrial smells is still commonplace.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Claudia Barrios Obregón from Kunak, the company behind the monitors in Des Moines, says: "Right now, the way that cities control or measure odours is olfactometry: a human panel measures and gives an opinion of what the odour is like.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: But that's not that realistic." The Spanish company's monitors are an example of so-called electronic noses that make it easier to detect smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Whatever technology is used, it can be hard to keep everyone happy, as smells are so subjective.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "Unfortunately, the general rule is that the nastier we perceive the odour to be, the more sensitive towards it we are," says Johan Lundström, a professor in the science of smell at the Karolinska Institute in Stockholm, Sweden.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Rhun ap Iorwerth delivered a speech about devolution to Cardiff University on Monday evening The Welsh government is to examine the powers councils have and how authorities work together regionally, the first minister has announced.

sentences.text: An AI tool may be able to help doctors judge how ill a patient is using a single photograph of their face, say US researchers.
sentences.article_title: Can a simple photo of your face reveal how ill you are?

sentences.text: Trained on millions of healthy faces, and 35,000 photos of cancer patients, the tool can make estimates on survival by looking closely at features near the eyes, the scientists say.

sentences.text: While it's a long way from being suitable for use in hospitals, the researchers say their goal is to help doctors recommend the right treatments for their patients.

sentences.article_title: Can a simple photo of your face reveal how ill you are?

sentences.text: The researchers developed two AI tools to estimate biological age and predict cancer survival from a single face photo.

sentences.article_title: Can a simple photo of your face reveal how ill you are?

sentences.text: These metrics applied across many different types of cancers, varying in severity, including ones that had spread to the patient's bones or brain.
